#3180. Linux Mint 27 arrives next month, and I like it already: New features and other upgrades to expect

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Tech > Services & Software > Operating Systems > Linux

It starts with a surprise version number: Linux Mint 27 instead of 24. But the next release brings far more changes than that.

Linux Mint, my favorite Linux desktop distribution, is ready for a fresh start.

Its lead developer, Clement “Clem” Lefebvre, announced earlier this year that the team behind it was considering slowing Mint’s release cadence because the old twice-a-year release cycle was time-consuming and constrained their ability to make major changes. So it is that the next release, Linux Mint 27, will appear in your Christmas stocking.

Also: 5 premium Linux distros absolutely worth paying for in 2026

The developers officially changed the designation on Oct. 13th when Mint changed both its release cadence and its numbering. Clem’s happy about the change: it “was a tough decision to make, but we’re really starting to see it pay off. We’re taking on projects and implementing changes which would previously have been considered too large or ambitious.”

The new Mint will use Ubuntu 26.04 Long Term Support (LTS) as its base. As before, it will offer Cinnamon, Xfce, and MATE desktops.

Earlier development snapshots had been labeled Mint 23 “Alfa.” That title was explicitly a placeholder while the team decided its release strategy. Its final name is Adrien. Moving ahead, release numbers will be based on the upcoming year. Clem said, “We’ll no longer use point releases, so the release after that will be 28. You’ll upgrade from 27 to 28 to 29, and so on.” Instead of girls’ names, Mint will use boys’ names for distro titles.

On Halloween, Clem announced the top changes in Mint 27. It starts with Mint bringing hibernation back into its supported desktop configuration through a dedicated Sleep Modes page in its System Administration tool. The page is intended to make enabling and configuring hibernation easier, including addressing its swap-space requirements.

It may not sound like much, but Clem explained it’s actually rather a big deal. “When you close the lid of your laptop, it goes into a sleep mode called “Suspend”. This mode is very useful… but it has a major limitation: It uses power.” People often forget it’s not really off and that your laptop will eventually run out of power. When that happens, “the outcome is worse than a normal shutdown. The session is gone, and the battery is empty.”

Also: Linux Mint vs. RefreshOS: I compared the two best distros for new users

That’s where “Hibernation comes into play. It saves the session to disk and completely shuts down the computer. No power is used. When you reopen the lid, the session is as it was, and so is the battery.”

Another new feature is Superlight. This fresh system-monitoring application replaces the older GNOME System Monitor. It comes with CPU, RAM, swap, GPU, network, disk I/O, temperature, and fan-speed graphs. It also includes per-application and per-process resource views. Battery-equipped systems also get charge and power-flow history.

Its storage analysis is particularly interesting: it can break down disk usage into files and folders, Steam games, and Flatpak applications. That brings several common troubleshooting tasks — “What’s using the CPU?” and “Where did my disk space go?” — into one interface. I’ve been checking it out on a Mint virtual machine (VM), and I like it already.

The Nemo file manager is getting a media preview pane, toggled with F7 or a status-bar button. It supports pictures, audio, and video, and displays associated information — for photographs, that can include the capture date and camera model. I like this feature a lot. I’ve always done a lot of work from file managers going all the way back to the classic Norton Commander and its Linux successor, Midnight Commander.

I’ve said it before, I’ll say it again. You don’t need to ever touch a Linux shell via a terminal to use Mint. But if, like me, you’re an old-school Linux user and you like using the terminal, Velocitty, Mint’s new terminal application, looks interesting. Its announced features include:

The point is to make recurring projects and SSH sessions easier to find and reopen. If you like other terminal programs, my latest fave is the Rust-based WexTerm; you don’t have to use Velocitty.

Unfold is a new archive manager for viewing, creating, and extracting archives. It uses 7-Zip and 7zip-RAR and supports the encryption formats those backends handle, including password-protected archives. Its design goal is simplicity rather than a sprawling feature set.

The new Mint uses Ubuntu 26.04 LTS as its foundation. Mint is also moving from Ubiquity to the Linux Mint Debian Edition live installer for installing the operating system. This fresh installer comes with support for OEM bulk-produced installations, installation on both BIOS and EFI PCs, support for Secure Boot, and LVM/LUKS configurations.

Also: Linux Mint vs. Zorin OS: I’ve tried both Windows alternatives, and here’s my winner

For the Linux kernel, Mint 27 will use version 7.0. Which one exactly? Good question. We’ll see closer to Christmas.

Wayland compatibility remains the goal, but X11 isn’t disappearing. As Clem said in June, “In an ideal scenario, we manage to make Wayland work just as well as X11.” But they’re not there yet.

The central change is a cleanup of existing code. Mint’s longer cycle gives developers room to overhaul several parts of the desktop together, rather than squeezing individual improvements into six-month windows. As Clem put it in the September newsletter, “I don’t think I’ve ever seen so many changes and new features implemented for a single release.”

What that means for you and me will be better laptop power management, more capable built-in utilities, and a more complete collection of everyday desktop applications. For example, I expect the updated Mint will ship with GIMP 3.2.2 as its default photo editor, instead of Mint 22.3’s years-old GIMP 2.10.

#3179. Apple Says There Are Now 100,000 Apps Built for the iPhone Duo

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

The new 4:3 inner screen doesn't play nicely with every app, but here's some that work so far.

Apple’s first foldable, the iPhone Duo, may have come last to the foldable party, as CNET’s review noted, but it’s certainly not least. Senior reporter Abrar Al-Heeti praised it for the iOS 27 integration across both displays and its impressive durability, which has crossed 300,000 folds in our test and counting.

However, as the Duo has filtered down to the general public, some new owners have noted that some of their favorite apps aren’t well optimized for the larger 4:3 inner display. I noticed this myself when I opened the iPhone Duo and launched Discord, finding the app centered on the screen with black space on both sides, rather than expanding to fill the panel.

That’s not unusual for a phone with a brand-new hardware design, and we’ve seen it on many Android foldables, with optimized apps taking a little bit of time to roll out. Apple has confirmed that this is already changing, with over 100,000 apps built for the iPhone Duo to more fully take advantage of the 4:3 main screen.

“Today, there are well over 100,000 apps built for iPhone Duo already live on the App Store, and thousands of optimized apps are being added to the store each day,” said Susan Prescott, Apple’s vice president of Worldwide Developer Relations in a comment sent to CNET.

“In the last month alone, thousands of developers have joined us for workshops in 19 cities around the world to experience iPhone Duo firsthand and bring updated apps to their users,” Prescott said. “The enthusiasm has been incredible, and we’re excited to see the pace of updates continue to accelerate as more and more apps optimize for iPhone Duo.”

Among the apps, Microsoft Word and Outlook have been adjusted to look similar to their desktop versions, while Zoom uses the inner display as a bigger video conference room. Additionally, the company has confirmed that sports fans can use the NBA and NHL apps to follow live games and highlights on the larger screen.

Etsy and LTK Creator will also show more products in the feed, and productivity apps like Goodnotes and Extra will make more use of the additional screen real estate. There’s also Halide Mark III, a pro camera app that adapts to every pose, from a viewfinder on the cover screen when closed to a waist-level viewfinder with one tap when half open.

The iOS 27.2 update should also add support for Apple Pencil (USB-C), letting Duo users in various compatible apps, like Apple Notes, work directly on documents.

Apple shared a list of apps that have been recently optimized for the iPhone Duo, breaking them down into categories like Work, AI, Finances, News and more.

This isn’t an exclusive list by any means. CNET previously confirmed seven iPhone Duo-ready apps that make the most of Apple’s foldable screen: Netflix, NYT Cooking, Fantastical, Edits by Instagram, TikTok, Instagram and Toastie.

Apple fans have put together their own “does it work on iPhone Duo?” web tracker, giving you a sense of whether an app is fully optimized, partially fits or is still awaiting updates. I can confirm that Discord is currently listed as “partially fits,” meaning it uses most of the inner screen but not all of it, which tracks with my own experience with the letterboxing.

We expect that this is only the beginning, and we’ll see the list above expand in the coming weeks as updated apps are submitted to the App Store. Going forward, you should also see spotlights for iPhone Duo apps in categories like “Great Apps and Games” and “Popular Apps.” Apple is making it easier to identify apps compatible with the iPhone Duo by adding a Made for iPhone Duo badge to product pages.

Jeremy Latcham does have a long history with the MCU

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

In a sudden and surprising move, DC Studios heads James Gunn and Peter Safran announced they were stepping down today (Nov. 11). The unexpected move (via Variety) comes just as Skydance acquired Warner Bros. Discovery for $111 billion in October.

The duo had led WB's attempt at revitalizing its comic book movies for the last four years and are being replaced by a former Marvel producer, Jeremy Latcham.

Under Gunn and Safran, it's been a mixed bag. Last year's "Superman" was a massive hit while this summer's "Supergirl" bombed out of the box office, even if we liked it more than most. However, the just-released body-horror R-rated "Clayface" has been a modest success.

In our Clayface review, we found Matt Hagen's performance and the practical effects entertaining, even if it didn't feel like a DC film. However, as Alix Blackburn noted, "I can't help feeling that “Clayface” leaves some serious potential untapped."

There are also the TV shows "Peacemaker" and "Lanterns", divisive but interesting projects that are worth your time.

So, who is Jeremy Latcham, and what does his hiring say about the future of the DC Universe?

Latcham only has 12 credits on his IMDB page, but he was on the ground floor at the beginning of the Marvel Cinematic Universe. Variety reports he joined Marvel in 2004 and worked his way up to an associate producer on "Iron Man" and a co-producer on "Iron Man 2."

Sign up to the weekly Tom's Streaming Guide to stay in the loop with the latest releases and top recommendations across your favorite streaming services. We’ve got you covered with a complete guide on what’s worth watching.

Later, he became an executive producer on the first and second Avengers movies as well as Guardians of the Galaxy and Spider-Man: Homecoming. Gunn directed and wrote the Guardians of the Galaxy trilogy.

"We’ve shared a creative history with Jeremy going back to Marvel, and we’re eager to see the perspective he brings to DC’s next chapter," Gunn and Safran said in a statement.

If there was a golden era of Marvel movies, the run from the first Iron Man to "Avengers: Endgame" is it, and Latcham was there for most of it, reportedly working closely with Marvel head Kevin Feige.

Latcham went solo around 2018 with the Tarantino-esque "Bad Times at the El Royale," which is too long and probably too clever by half, but a solid evening. He also produced the D&D movie "Honor Among Thieves," a personal favorite even if it didn't set the box office on fire.

That movie came out in 2023, and Latcham's most recent credit is the deeply boring Nate Bargatze vehicle "The Breadwinner."

I suspect Latcham is expected to bring a Marvel structure and formula to the DC Universe, which has been scattershot even under Gunn.

The difference between the DC Universe and what Marvel has built over the last 18 years is the characters. DC is defined by inherently mythological heroes, whereas Marvel, outside of some of its more operatic teams, has tended to be more character-driven.

It makes for archetypes that people have strong opinions about, and I'm not sold on the idea that the Marvel formula can work with the myths of DC. As with Marvel, DC's best successes have come from characters that aren't part of the holy trinity or the Justice League, à la Peacemaker or Gunn's Suicide Squad, and I guess the first Shazam.

We're still waiting for the delayed "The Batman: Part 2" with Robert Pattinson, which paused production in October as director Matt Reeves deals with a family matter.

James Gunn's is directing his Superman follow up "Man of Tomorrow." And on the TV side of things, "The People v. Gorilla Grodd" show is expected to launch in 2027 starring Jimmy Teatro and Skyler Gisondo.

It may be a year or two before we really see what Latcham has in store for the DC Universe.

ZDNET’s Lance Whitney recommends using Siri AI’s onscreen awareness feature to ask it for directions, explain something you see on your phone’s screen, or to add items from your screen to a list. He also uses Siri AI to edit his photos simply by asking for the changes he wants. But that’s just skimming the surface. You can read more about Whitney’s experiences using Siri AI here.

iOS 27 delivered Siri AI in beta this fall, along with iPadOS 27, MacOS 27 Golden Gate, VisionOS 27, and WatchOS 27.

You need a compatible iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, or Apple Vision Pro to use Apple Intelligence features like Siri AI. Not all Apple devices that support the latest iOS 27 (or other OS 27) will support Siri AI.

#3176. iPhone Duo vs. Galaxy Z Fold 8 Camera Comparison: Frolicking With Apple’s and Samsung’s Foldables

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

I snapped some photos in a dreamy garden with these passport-size phones to see how their rear cameras stack up.

There are a handful of things Apple’s iPhone Duo and Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 have in common. They both feature a passport-size design, two rear cameras and roughly the same battery capacity. They’re also two of my favorite phones I’ve reviewed this year.

The compact, book-style configuration feels like the future of foldables, and Apple and Samsung have each nailed their offerings. Both phones are incredibly versatile, giving you the option to quickly swipe through apps on the palm-sized cover display or open up to a more sprawling 7.6-inch inner screen that’s great for watching videos and multitasking. That innovation comes at a cost, though, with the Duo starting at $1,999 for 256GB and the Z Fold 8 starting at $1,900 for the same storage level.

There are some drawbacks to having a more compact design, namely when it comes to the rear cameras. There’s no telephoto camera on either phone, which can make the high price tags a little harder to swallow. Plus, the wide and ultra-wide cameras aren’t quite as capable as what you’ll get on premium non-folding phones such as the iPhone 18 Pro and Galaxy S26 Ultra, which have more advanced optical zoom capabilities and larger main-camera sensors.

Still, the iPhone Duo’s and Z Fold 8’s cameras are nothing to scoff at. The Duo has a 48-megapixel wide and 48-megapixel ultrawide camera, as well as a 12-megapixel selfie camera on the cover screen and a FaceTime camera on the inner display (Apple hasn’t shared the resolution). Meanwhile, the Z Fold 8 has a 50-megapixel wide and 50-megapixel ultrawide camera, plus 10-megapixel selfie cameras on the cover and inner displays. That means you should still get photos that impress, whether you’re in the brightly lit outdoors or in a dark, moody setting.

To compare the cameras, I took the iPhone Duo and Galaxy Z Fold 8 to Filoli, a historic house and garden in the San Francisco Bay Area. These are some of my favorite shots, highlighting the strengths and unique characteristics of each phone’s cameras.

Both phones do a great job depicting the vibrancy of the lush background, but the iPhone Duo has the edge here. It better preserves the detail in the stone bench and flooring, and the greenery takes on a deeper, more satisfying hue.

These photos turned out very similarly, and both are equally dazzling. But the Z Fold 8 image is slightly sharper, as seen in the lines on the tree bark and the brighter, more pigmented greenery and flora. So I’m giving this one to the Z Fold 8.

These portrait images highlight some of the key differences in color and tone between the iPhone Duo and Galaxy Z Fold 8. I prefer the richer blacks and more vibrant colors captured by the iPhone Duo. It also does a better job of keeping the raven in focus, allowing the bird to stand out more distinctly against the background and creating a more striking overall image. By comparison, the Z Fold 8 produces a softer, gentler look, with a more subdued overall tone.

I like the brightness of the iPhone Duo image, and while the Z Fold 8 shot has slightly deeper shadows, the hydrangeas are also more vibrant. The blues and greens pop more on the Z Fold 8, as does the sky, which is a little washed out on the Duo. So this one goes to the Z Fold 8.

I keep flipping on this one, but ultimately, the richer colors and texture on the Duo image have won me over. The iPhone’s camera tends to cast a warmer glow, as you can see in the stone benches, while the Z Fold 8 takes on a more neutral tone. In the end, the differences are subtle and a matter of personal preference.

And finally, here’s me unwinding with a book. By default, the iPhone Duo applies a pleasing background blur, which I appreciate for the added dramatic effect. (This effect can be disabled when taking a photo, but I rarely choose to do so.) The Z Fold 8, by comparison, keeps the distant lawns and forested hills in sharper focus, preserving those details remarkably well. Ultimately, I prefer the Duo’s approach, which keeps the book in sharper focus and makes it stand out from the background. That said, I do appreciate the Z Fold 8’s ability to capture finer details throughout the scene, particularly the crisp individual blades of grass.

Because I’m a fan of both the iPhone Duo and the Galaxy Z Fold 8, it’s difficult to wholeheartedly recommend one camera over the other. Each has its strengths, and there are moments where one preserves detail and color better than the other.

In general, photos from the iPhone Duo tend to have warmer tones and richer, deeper colors, which can also lead to more pronounced shadows. Meanwhile, the Galaxy Z Fold 8 often produces brighter images, though this can sometimes come at the expense of finer details. But these results can vary depending on factors such as lighting and angles.

Ultimately, both foldable phones deliver impressive results, and the choice comes down to which image characteristics you value most. Thankfully, you really can’t go wrong with either.

#3174. 3 ways Bluetooth 7 upgrades your devices beyond lossless audio

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Bluetooth Core 7.0 could make your smart home devices easier to set up, for one. Here's what we know about the new core specification.

Bluetooth Core 7.0 is here, and each new specification from the Bluetooth Special Interest Group (SIG) offers a glimpse of what we can expect from our devices in the future. The major feature incorporated into the new core standard is High Data Throughput (HDT), which can enable lossless wireless audio and improved multi-channel spatial audio on more Bluetooth devices.

Also: Apple has a Bluetooth problem, and Android is taking advantage

Bluetooth Core 7.0’s standout feature is that it can achieve wireless lossless audio. However, the improvements to the Bluetooth stack architecture — particularly, expanding the Bluetooth spectrum — allow for faster data transfer, improved energy efficiency, more resilient connections, and create more room for devices and their data-intensive applications.

HDT means good news for audiophiles, smart home enthusiasts, VR/XR fans, wellness wearable aficionados, AI companion devotees, and much more. I explained applications of HDT in a wireless audio context earlier this year. Now that it’s officially adopted, here’s what you can expect.

A major milestone in Bluetooth Core 7.0 is the ability to stream lossless audio over a wireless connection. Bluetooth is lossy, requiring data compression that diminishes audio quality. HDT’s faster data transfer and greater wireless data capacity enable it to handle the massive volume of data required to achieve lossless quality.

Also: Your Bose headphones are getting a major Bluetooth upgrade – what to expect

Audiophiles typically avoid wireless headphones for intensive listening due to the necessary data compression, opting for wired headphones that can accommodate larger lossless files. Bluetooth’s innovation here is widely regarded as a major leap in wireless technology.

HDT also promises to standardize spatial audio, with expanded data transfers allowing for multi-channel audio setups. Standardizing this form of audio transmission could mean consumers can expect more affordable brands and products to adopt this premium feature.

Every consumer-friendly feature possible within Bluetooth Core 7.0 can be traced back to its ability to accommodate more devices and their ever-expanding data needs. According to a Bluetooth blog post, Bluetooth HDT delivers nearly four times the previous maximum Bluetooth throughput.

Data throughput is the amount of data received, transmitted, and processed over the Bluetooth network. With nearly four times the processing power, HDT can move more data, faster. HDT increases Bluetooth’s maximum supported bitrate to 7.5 Mbps, up from the current 2 Mbps.

Also: Beware of Bluetooth sniffers: How your favorite gadgets could be exposing your data

The result is shorter download times for a device’s firmware update, faster device location when Find My Device is activated, or faster transfer of a large photo album via Android’s QuickShare or Apple’s AirDrop.

In the same blog post, Øyvind Strøm, executive vice president of the short-range business unit at Nordic Semiconductor, gives examples of a smartwatch syncing hours’ worth of workout data to your phone in seconds, or a pair of headphones, a smart speaker, or a security camera that can download a firmware update with nearly zero interruption to the user experience.

In a smart home context, Bluetooth Low Energy (LE) is the wireless technology that works in the background, connecting your devices. Bluetooth LE is the baseline technology for quick device discovery and connection. The most recent example of this is Apple’s HomeView, which uses Bluetooth LE to discover a nearby, trusted iPhone to unlock that user’s personalized home hub display.

The less you feel its presence through lags, wait times, and dropouts, the better it’s working. HDT’s goal is to make Bluetooth connectivity frictionless, which is especially valuable when your smart lights, shades, speakers, TVs, refrigerators, and more rely on the technology.

Also: Forget Wi-Fi: Apple is betting on Bluetooth with its new home devices

For example, HDT’s improved data throughput could allow doorbells, cameras, and robot vacuums to quickly offload large amounts of data to your smart home hub. It could also enable near-instantaneous setup of a new device onto your smart home network and firmware updates.

Finally, HDT also addressed network stability and reliability, especially in high-traffic areas such as apartment complexes and dense cities, where a busy network can cause delays and backups. Alongside improvements to Wi-Fi and Thread, a truly seamless smart home is on the horizon.

Bluetooth’s Human Interface Device (HID) profile refers to the wireless communication used by peripheral devices, such as mice, keyboards, and game controllers, when connecting to a host device. Smart glasses and controllers connected to XR/VR headsets also use this profile, and their data-intensive computing will benefit greatly from HDT.

Devices using the HID profile can expect HDT to lay the foundation for making cloud gaming more reliable, spatial computing more responsive, and offloading audio/visual data from smart glasses less power-intensive.

Also: Frustrated with your Bluetooth? How multipoint works – and why it sometimes won’t

Additionally, gaming keyboards and mice can expect HDT’s expanded data processing to deliver shorter device communication intervals, reducing latency and lag.

In 2026, we’re starting to see more Bluetooth Core 6.0-equipped devices, with Samsung’s recently announced Galaxy Buds On featuring Bluetooth 6.2. Though Bluetooth’s blog post states that the first application of HDT will be for premium wireless audio, many audio manufacturers are behind, still releasing products with Bluetooth 5.4.

Smartphones, smartwatches, and smart home products tend to move a little faster, with the majority of current Bluetooth Core 6.0 products falling into these categories.

The Bluetooth SIG announced Auracast in 2022, and audio manufacturers are now beginning to adopt this technology more widely. Channel Sounding was released with Bluetooth Core 6.0 in 2024, with some early adopters releasing compatible products this year, including Google’s Pixel Tag and Motorola’s Moto Tag 2; more are expected next year and into 2028. With these adoption cycles in mind, we may be well into the next decade before HDT becomes standard.

Fans of the Roku aquarium will need to find a new way to just keep swimming.

Roku users are about to feel like fish out of water, as fans of the platform’s classic Aquatic Life screensaver are discovering that the animation will soon be unavailable.

The popular animated screensaver featuring realistic aquarium life will be replaced by the Roku City screensaver on Dec. 1. Roku City is the platform’s signature purple skyline, featuring rotating digital billboards packed with brand sponsorships and clever pop-culture Easter eggs. (Seattle’s short-spined raccoon, Jimothy, has made an appearance.)

That doesn’t mean all fish-filled options have been flushed. Several third-party Roku wallpaper apps offer a variety of aquarium options to choose from. But if you’re sticking to what Roku itself provides on its streaming boxes, the move away from the aquarium screensaver also means switching to an alternative that’s filled with advertising.

A Roku representative didn’t respond to a request for comment.

Viewers who miss these specific fish can still watch a YouTube version of Roku’s Aquatic Life screensaver for as long as the company chooses to keep this nearly 3-minute video on the internet.

The Aquatic Life screensaver loss is a drop in the ocean compared to other changes at the streamer this year. Roku was purchased by Fox for $22 billion in June, which puts the streaming platform under the same ownership as Fox’s Tubi and Fox One channels. That deal is expected to close in 2027.

#3172. BlackRock's Rick Rieder sees 'historic' opportunity in high-quality bonds

Investors may be wary of the volatility hitting parts of the bond market right now, but they have an "historic" opportunity to grab attractive yields in high-quality credit, Rick Rieder, BlackRock's chief investment officer for global fixed income, told CNBC in an exclusive interview.

Hypothetically, it's now possible for investors to build a diversified portfolio that yields more than 7% with less than three years of duration and an average credit quality of A-, he said. Duration is a measurement of a bond's price sensitivity to fluctuations in rates, and issues with shorter maturities tend to have lower duration.

"Not only is it historic in that these yields are where they are, but the only time these yields are ever here is when there's some problem, like an economic problem or default problem," Rieder said in an interview about his fourth-quarter outlook, released Wednesday.

That isn't the case now, where the economy remains strong, he said. "So you don't really have to worry about defaults of any significance."

While Rieder didn't specifically identify the credits in the aforementioned portfolio, the iShares Aaa - A Rated Corporate Bond ETF (QLTA) has a 30-day SEC yield of 5.68% and an effective duration of 6.48 years — higher than Rieder's low duration focus.

The iShares Flexible Income Active ETF (BINC), which is managed by Rieder, has a 5.66% 30-day SEC yield and three-year effective duration, but its portfolio extends beyond investment-grade credit.

Rieder sees the best opportunity right now in investment-grade corporate bonds — which he pointed out he hasn't said "in a really long time." Investment grade bonds are rated AAA through BBB- by S&P and Fitch, while Moody's rates them Aaa through Baa3.

That includes hyperscaler bonds, which have flooded the market with issuance this year as they ramp up their AI infrastructure. Alphabet, Amazon, Meta Platforms and Oracle have issued a total of about $228.4 billion in bonds year to date, as of Oct. 20, according to LSEG.

"They're very low leverage. They have tremendous amounts of cash flow coming in," Rieder said of the hyperscalers in general. "You're now getting to buy these entities which are higher quality, paying you a very attractive yield to get it."

Rieder's iShares Flexible Income Active ETF has upped its allocation to investment-grade corporates to 14.3% of its portfolio. In July, that stood at 8.5%.

That said, investors need to be patient and sit tight since rates could still move higher from here, he advised.

"Your starting point is by far your best barometer of what your return is going to be," he noted. "So if you get seven and a quarter, maybe you get eight, maybe you get six, but ... if your holding period is a year or longer, you're going to get that yield."

Caution should also be exercised outside of investment-grade credit, which requires more selectivity and deep research, he warned. That includes AI names.

"There's parts of the data center supply that's not hyperscaler guaranteed or hyperscaler backed," he said. "That we've been more cautious around, and we'll continue to be."

The bond market, particularly high-yield credit, has been rocked as investor concern grows over the massive amount of debt some companies are taking out to fund their artificial intelligence build-out.

Junk-rated CoreWeave has become the poster child, seeing its stock drop, bond yields jump and credit-default spreads widen. Oracle, which is sitting in the lower end of investment grade and is seen as a bellwether on the broader AI market, has also taken some hits.

Rieder is also keeping an eye on the Federal Reserve, which is expected to raise its federal funds rate again in December to combat inflation. The market is currently pricing in a nearly 90% probability that the central bank will hike at that time, according to the CME Group FedWatch tool.

The money manager expects that to happen, although he does not agree with it. Higher rates are hurting parts of the economy, like housing, while not having much of an impact on other areas — such as tech companies' capital expenditures, which have become a big driver of growth, he said.

"They're not borrowing off the overnight funds rate," Rieder noted. "There's a lot of floating rate finance in housing, credit card, auto loan finance, and you're seeing those areas already under pressure."

Instead, the market is and will continue to price the AI supply coming into the market, he added.

Rieder sees a number of possible risks ahead, including rising levels of government debt across the globe. In the United States, the budget deficit has grown to $2 trillion for fiscal 2026.

"The more the central banks raise the rates, the cost of debt to these to already indebted governments is something we've got to be careful about over time," he said.

Bond supply coming from AI companies should also be watched.

"With the amount of supply that's coming — data center, hyperscaler — there's some crowding-out effect that's taking place," he said. "With government rates moving higher, that is something that we just got to keep an eye on."

In the meantime, Rieder would just continue to reap the rewards of high investment-grade yields "and smile a lot," he said.

#3170. Claude’s new Personal Finance tool aims to help analyze your spending – read-only, of course

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Anthropic has released what appears to be its answer to ChatGPT Finances.

You can now share your financial information with Claude and ask the chatbot for insights on your spending.

Also: Researchers asked people to use AI chatbots for election info

Personal Finance in Claude, which Anthropic announced Thursday, reviews your connected accounts through read-only access via Plaid. That security measure follows OpenAI’s equivalent feature, ChatGPT Finances, which launched in May. Here’s what to know.

Functionally, this feature appears similar to ChatGPT Finances: It lets you link as many bank and credit card accounts as you’d like to Claude via Plaid with read-only access. You can then ask Claude where you spent your money this month or whether you can afford to take a vacation in six months, for example.

(Disclosure: Ziff Davis, ZDNET’s parent company, filed an April 2025 lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging it infringed Ziff Davis copyrights in training and operating its AI systems.)

Also: Stop sharing your passwords with AI agents

According to Anthropic, the feature is a response to existing use patterns: the company’s April usage report found that financial advice was one of the main topics users ask Claude for help with.

“For the accounts you choose to connect (and only those), Claude sees the bank’s name, each account’s name, type, and last four digits, balances and credit limits, and up to two years of transactions. When you chat with Claude in the Personal Finance hub, those conversations aren’t used to train our models.”

The idea behind the feature is that you can ask follow-up questions and request more insights about spending habits, trends over time, and future goals based on what Claude finds, similar to any other Claude conversation. The tool will also generate tables and charts to visualize your financial information.

“You can ask for a weekly spending chart, a calendar of what’s due, or a dashboard of the numbers you choose, and Claude builds it as an artifact you can keep adjusting and coming back to,” an Anthropic representative told ZDNET via email.

Also: I connected ChatGPT to my bank, and it’s my go-to finance app now

You can also expect an ad-free experience in the feature.

“Like the rest of Claude, Personal Finance has no ads or sponsored recommendations, and it doesn’t offer credit cards, loans, or savings accounts of its own, so your money questions get a straight answer,” the company said in the announcement.

The company added that because Claude is using actual transaction data and not memory, the feature shouldn’t hallucinate.

“It can list the exact transactions behind any number so you can check its math,” Anthropic said via email. “Like any AI, it can make mistakes, so for anything important, we recommend confirming with your bank.”

Still, the difference — and for many, the appeal — here is the natural language interface. Other finance apps don’t necessarily have an easy, accessible chat function where users can shoot off quick questions like they would to a human financial planner. These assistants also present historical budget analysis in plain English, rather than requiring users to interpret dashboards themselves, which users may see as a perk.

Also: 5 ways to use AI when your budget is tight

On Reddit, many users find ChatGPT Finances to be accurate and reliable. One Reddit user said ChatGPT Finance seemed to have Mint or Monarch potential, but noted it was still “weaker” than those apps in some areas, such as historical syncing, high-quality dashboards, and generating full statement PDFs.

“ChatGPT has genuinely helped me make better financial decisions,” she wrote.

Anthropic noted that users shouldn’t look to Personal Finance for Claude as a total authority. “Personal Finance is a first step. For life’s bigger money decisions, we think people are best served by Claude working alongside the licensed professionals and regulated firms they trust,” the company said in the announcement.

“We’re exploring how to make that possible in Claude, and we’d like to hear from banks, wealth managers, and financial services companies who want to help shape it” — indicating a more integrated financial planning system within Claude may be on the way.

#3169. Motorcar Parts (MPAA) Q2 2027 Earnings Call Transcript

Delayed orders hit sales, but new awards point to a stronger second half.

Motorcar Parts of America, Inc. (MPAA -26.62%) reported a decrease in quarterly revenue attributed to delayed customer orders and lower tariff pass-throughs, prompting management to lower its full-year sales guidance. Despite these near-term headwinds, the company secured significant new business awards and completed a strategic manufacturing relocation to Mexico to improve cost structures. Management expects a stronger second half of the fiscal year as new programs launch and inventory liquidations from competitors subside. The company remains focused on leveraging its diagnostic technology and expanding its brake product line to drive long-term market share gains.

Operator: Hello, everyone. Thank you for joining us, and welcome to the Motorcar Parts of America, Inc. Fiscal 2027 Second Quarter Conference Call. The Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995 provides a safe harbor for certain forward-looking statements, including statements made during today's conference call regarding future financial performance, sales growth, margin improvement, operating efficiencies, customer demand, new business strategies, capacity utilization, working capital liquidity, debt levels, cash flows, strategic initiatives and market conditions. These statements are based on current expectations, estimates, forecasts and assumptions and are not guarantees of future performance.

Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied in these forward-looking statements due to risks and uncertainties, including changes in customer ordering patterns, customer concentration, competitive conditions, supply chain constraints, inflation, tariffs, interest rates, credit availability, labor and production costs, inventory levels, operational execution and macroeconomic conditions and other risks described in the company's most recent Form 10-K, 10-Q and other filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission. The company undertakes no obligation to update or revise any forward-looking statements, except as required by law. For a more detailed discussion of some of our ongoing risks and uncertainties of the company's business, I refer you to the various filings.

With that, I'd like to begin the call and turn the call over to Selwyn Joffe.

Selwyn Joffe: Thank you, Gary. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us. As outlined in our earnings release this morning, our second quarter results reflect delayed customer orders. There were also delayed orders relating to the realignment of inventory at certain customer distribution centers. Also, there were lower tariff pass-throughs compared with the prior year. While these conditions have affected our near-term performance, we remain confident in the underlying fundamentals of our industry and most importantly, in the substantial opportunities we are developing to expand our business and improve profitability. I want to focus today on several developments that we believe will strengthen Motorcar Parts of America's competitive position and provide a foundation for meaningful future growth.

First, we have secured nearly $60 million in incremental annualized new business awards from both existing and new customers. These awards represent product programs we were not previously supplying with anticipated annual volumes based on customer requirements and historical sales activity. This is an important distinction. We are not simply forecasting opportunities. We have been awarded business that we expect to translate into additional revenue as the programs launch and mature. Small initial shipments have already commenced, and we expect all these programs to launch during the second half of this fiscal 2027, with the majority of these programs launching towards fiscal year-end.

We also currently anticipate approximately $25 million in incremental annualized sales by the end of March, with additional contributions expected as these programs ramp during fiscal 2028. We believe these awards demonstrate our ability to gain market share even during a period of softer industry demand. Turning to our Brake business. Brakes have become our second major product category, building on more than 50 years of experience and our established leadership in rotating electrical products. We believe this is particularly attractive because Brakes represent an essential nondiscretionary wear category with multiple replacement opportunities over the life of the vehicle.

Our brake-related product offerings, including calipers, pads, rotors, master cylinders, power boosters, wheel hubs and brake shoes provide opportunities to expand our relationships with major retailers and professional aftermarket customers. The relaunch of our Centric Parts brand represents an important additional opportunity. Centric is an established name in the professional brake aftermarket, and we believe that combining that brand with our existing manufacturing capabilities, product coverage and distribution infrastructure significantly strengthens our competitive position. Importantly, potential Centric sales are not included in our current incremental growth estimates. We also believe increased utilization of our existing brake manufacturing capacity can contribute to improved operating leverage and profitability as these volumes grow.

We are also encouraged by the expansion of our business opportunities beyond the United States. Mexico is becoming an increasingly important growth market for us. Some of our largest customers are expanding their operations there, creating additional opportunities for Motorcar Parts of America to supply products through our established relationships, capability and performance. Some of these opportunities are included in our current new business expectations, while others represent additional potential growth. We also see opportunities as major aftermarket customers expand geographically into Canada. Our established North American relationships, combined with our manufacturing and distribution capabilities provide a strong platform to support these exciting developments. Turning to our heavy-duty rotating electric business.

We have completed the relocation of this operation from Canada into our existing manufacturing facility in Mexico, where production has commenced. This initiative is an important part of our continuing efforts to improve our manufacturing competitiveness. By leveraging existing infrastructure, manufacturing resources and operating capabilities, we expect to reduce costs, improve production efficiencies and benefit from operating synergies. We believe this will strengthen our competitive position in the heavy-duty aftermarket and improve our ability to pursue additional business. Another business demonstrating continued positive momentum is our rotating electric diagnostic testing equipment program. Our JBT-1 diagnostic testing equipment has an established presence with major automotive aftermarket customers across the United States, Mexico and Canada.

We continue to expand installations within existing customer networks while pursuing additional opportunities, including international markets. We believe there is significant long-term potential for broader deployment of this technology throughout the automotive aftermarket. Stepping back, we remain constructive about the long-term fundamentals of the automotive aftermarket. The average age of vehicles on the road continues to increase and consumers are keeping their vehicles longer. Higher new vehicle prices also reinforce the economic incentive to maintain and repair existing vehicles. These dynamics are particularly relevant to our business because we supply essential components required for vehicles to start, stop and operate safely. Although repairs and purchases can be deferred temporarily, the underlying need for replacement parts remains.

While we see temporary deferrals, we believe that a catch-up is ahead as the economy stabilizes. We believe our broad product coverage, manufacturing capabilities, customer relationships and global operating platform uniquely position us to participate and meet the long-term demand. In summary, while the current operating environment remains challenging, we are making progress on several important fronts. We have secured significant incremental new business. We are expanding our brake platform through Centric. We are pursuing additional opportunities as major customers expand geographically. Our rotating electrical diagnostic business continues to gain momentum, and we have completed an important heavy-duty manufacturing relocation designed to improve our competitiveness. These developments are not dependent solely on an industry recovery.

They reflect initiatives we are undertaking to strengthen our market position and improve our long-term operating performance. We remain focused on converting these opportunities, improving manufacturing utilization, generating cash flow and delivering sustainable profitability. With that, I will turn the call over to David to review our financial results and updated outlook.

David Lee: Thank you, Selwyn, and good morning, everyone. Let's start with analytics for the fiscal second quarter. Fiscal second quarter ended September 30, 2026, net sales of $169.2 million were impacted by delayed customer orders and a reduction in tariff pass-throughs. Broader economic uncertainty, including inflation, tariffs and uneven consumer spending also contributed to a cautious operating environment. Additionally, net sales for the prior year reflect $14.8 million of core revenue in connection with the realignment of inventory at certain customer distribution centers. We believe higher sales and a continued focus on efficiency and cost reductions will favorably continue to favorably contribute to results for the second half of fiscal 2027.

From a sales perspective, as sales momentum increases, combined with new business commitments that Selwyn referenced earlier, which has had a small impact through September 30, 2026, as well as other meaningful opportunities, we believe the company will benefit in several ways near term, including favorable impact to gross margin, continued annual cash flow generation, net debt reduction and opportunities to increase shareholder value. In short, we believe the fundamentals of our business are strong. Regarding gross margin, let me first discuss the second quarter in more detail. Gross margin was 24.2% compared with 19.3% a year earlier.

Gross margin was impacted by noncash expenses of 2.8 percentage points and benefited from onetime items of 5.7 percentage points, including approximately $11.1 million of IEEPA tariff refunds as detailed in Exhibit 3 of this morning's earnings press release. In addition, gross margin was impacted by unfavorable foreign exchange rates of approximately 1.4 percentage points or approximately $2.4 million due to the weakening of the U.S. dollar versus the Mexican peso. Excluding the noncash expenses and onetime items as well as the foreign exchange impact, gross margin was approximately 22.7% for the quarter. Fiscal 2027 gross margin is expected to be favorably impacted by increased sales and overall cost reductions and efficiencies.

Overall, regarding gross margin, we remain focused on overall margin accretion supported by strong momentum and greater utilization of brake-related capacity from both existing and new business. We are also focused on positive impacts to overall margin from further improvements in operating efficiencies supported by benefiting from our tariff mitigation initiatives, better pricing for scrap sales as we gain more market share for our products, additional opportunities to relocate certain operations to our low-cost facilities globally, including Mexico and further strategic cost reductions. These initiatives are expected to positively impact overall gross margin.

Our cash flow, balance sheet and liquidity for the quarter was impacted by working capital inventory ramp-up for new business, and we used cash in operating activities of approximately $4.1 million for the second quarter. The company's revolver loan of $126.6 million, less cash of $20.8 million at September 30, 2026, resulted in net bank debt of $105.8 million. For the prior 3 years ended March 31, 2026, the company generated cash from operating activities of approximately $103.8 million. While quarters fluctuate, the company continues to expect to generate positive cash flow. Our liquidity of total cash plus revolver availability was approximately $104.8 million as of September 30, 2026.

We remain focused on increasing operating profit and gross margin and generating positive cash flow, supported by growth and operating efficiencies from our global footprint. In addition to our goal of generating increased operating profits, including benefits from our gross margin expansion initiatives previously explained, we expect further opportunities to neutralize working capital, supported by customer product demand planning, enhanced inventory management and extending our vendor payment terms, including growing our supply chain finance program offered to our vendors. Recently, MPA received a highly commended award in the category for best use of supply chain finance by a leading provider of supply chain programs.

Regarding our debt leverage, based on information in our filing today, EBITDA for the 12 months ended September 30, 2026, was $58.9 million. EBITDA before the impact of noncash and onetime cash items was approximately $70 million for the same period. To recap, our net bank debt was $105.8 million at September 30, 2026, compared with EBITDA before the impact of noncash and onetime cash items mentioned above of $70 million for the 12 months ended September 30, 2026, resulting in a net bank debt-to-EBITDA ratio of 1.5. I should mention that under the company's authorized share repurchase program, there was approximately $20.1 million available to repurchase shares at September 30, 2026. Turning to our outlook.

We are revising our fiscal 2027 guidance to reflect delayed customer orders in both our existing business and contributions from new business awards. For the fiscal year ending March 31, 2027, we now expect net sales of $715 million to $740 million compared with our previous guidance of $780 million to $800 million. The revised outlook reflects a challenging ordering environment and the timing of new program launches. As Selwyn discussed, we expect all of the awarded programs to launch during the second half, with most launching toward fiscal year-end and continuing to ramp during fiscal 2028. We expect full year operating income of $37 million to $44 million.

This outlook reflects approximately $30 million in noncash expenses, approximately $5 million in expenses associated with relocating our heavy-duty operations to Mexico and excluding approximately $11 million in IEEPA tariff refunds recognized in the second quarter. In addition, full year depreciation and amortization is estimated at approximately $9 million. To put the revised outlook into perspective, our guidance implies second half net sales of $378 million to $403 million. This compares with $380 million in the prior year period, representing a decline of approximately 0.5% to growth of approximately 6.1%. The prior year second half included $19.9 million in core revenue in connection with the realignment of inventory at certain customer distribution centers.

Excluding that revenue from the prior year comparison, our projected second half sales represent growth of approximately 5% to 11.9%. We expect second half operating income of $23 million to $30 million, reflecting approximately $14 million in noncash expenses. In addition, second half depreciation and amortization is estimated at approximately $5 million. Our expected second half improvement is supported by contributions from new business, better utilization of our manufacturing capacity and continued cost reductions and operating efficiencies. While the timing of customer orders remain a source of uncertainty, our focus is clear: execute the scheduled launches, improve margins and convert sales to cash. With that, we will open the call for questions.

Operator: Your first question comes from the line of Brian Nagel with Oppenheimer.

Brian Nagel: I was hoping, Selwyn, you could just go into more detail with the -- I guess, I would always call the sales dislocations that happened here in the quarter and then we've given the guidance look like they'll persist through the balance of the year. You mentioned -- I guess, activity on part of your customers and then some tariff dynamic. But I guess the first one is you just want more detail on what happened here and what disrupted so significantly the sales run rates?

Selwyn Joffe: Yes. So let me sort of focus on three major points. We had a reallocation where we moved our business opportunities from certain warehouses to newer different warehouses. The ramp-up in the newer warehouses is, I think, the economy affected, but the number of stores in those newer warehouses has been slower than was anticipated. We believe that's going to catch up. So what happens is you lose -- you give up certain warehouses and you get certain warehouses and that ramps up slower, I mean, there's a sort of gap between the revenue. Now we're starting to see that change.

Just as a matter of backdrop, Brian, is that certainly in the last 4 weeks, we're seeing more vibrancy coming back to the entire categories that we're in. So that was number one. Then number two is we picked up a nice amount of new business from the First Brands' bankruptcy or liquidation in the brake business. And in that brake business, what happened is that the First Brands' inventory got -- it was being liquidated. And so a number of the existing customers bought inventory in that liquidation. So that deferred the ramp-up volume in what we received. Now we think that, that's substantially over, and we're receiving that now.

We're receiving that now, and we think that, that is going to be vibrant. And then last but not least is we've had some softening in the -- just in basically in the fundamentals, mostly in the DIY business. We're a big supplier to the DIY business, and some of those orders have got deferred. Now we're starting again to see some more vibrancy in that area. And those are the 3 major items that really somewhat took us by surprise. I mean, we saw a couple of months of really soft revenue and then it came -- has come back now, and we're hoping to see that continue.

Brian Nagel: So as a follow-up to that, to the first point there with regard to, I guess, the warehouse movement, is this one customer? Or is this something you're seeing more pervasive through the sector?

Selwyn Joffe: That is one customer. That's one customer. That particular event is one customer. If you had to look in general, I'd say across the spectrum, we're seeing some softness. Again, in general, we're seeing a pickup as well across the spectrum.

Brian Nagel: Oh, go ahead. Sorry to interrupt. Go ahead.

Selwyn Joffe: No, no. I mean, I think in general, I mean, that certain customers are weaker than others. But in general, that's the trend.

Brian Nagel: And then I guess maybe more for David. So you had this -- I'm going to use the word dislocation here in the fiscal second quarter, but you took down guidance substantially for the year itself, and I hear you saying trends got better maybe in the last month of the fiscal quarter. So as you're thinking about the guidance and the thinking behind that guidance, what's embedded there? Is this reflect basically the weakness that was in the earlier part of the quarter? Or is it all embedded in some of the pickup we're seeing or saw late in the quarter?

Selwyn Joffe: No, I think what you're seeing in the guidance, and I'll turn it over to David, is that the first 6 months, obviously was significantly weaker than we thought, but we believe the back 6 months is going to return. So David, I'll turn it over to you to talk more about that.

David Lee: That's a good question. We're already seeing October sales have increased compared to the end of the trend in fiscal second quarter, and we expect that trend to continue. So we're already seeing orders pick up.

Selwyn Joffe: Yes. And I think that the guidance, we're assuming that the tide for our existing business will increase, but not all the way. We do think it's going to get stronger. And then the significant amount of new business that's coming on will further enhance that. So I mean, the question is how high is the tide going to come back to -- is it going to come back to our normal or even greater because there is, I think, some discussion in the industry that there may be some catch-up because these are -- when you say nondiscretionary, I mean, people are delaying these repairs.

Their cars don't work, but they're not scrapping their vehicles because they're not replacing a component in the vehicle. So there's a potential for some tailwinds catching up, but we're not assuming all of that. We're being -- we do think that there is a recovery coming, but not -- we're not assuming a significant tailwind at this point, but there is a possibility of that.

Operator: Your next question comes from the line of Derek Soderberg with Cantor Fitzgerald.

Derek Soderberg: So I wanted to start with the new business, the $60 million. I was curious how fast you can ramp that opportunity. It sounds like some of it is going to start shipping by the end of the fiscal year. But I was just wondering if you can kind of talk about how fast you can really ramp to that $60 million level. And then the $25 million announcement on new business, is that related to the $60 million? Is that the same kind of group of customers, same products? Can you talk a little bit more about the $25 million piece as well?

Selwyn Joffe: Yes. So the $60 million is firm commitments that we have right now. That's annualized revenue. We believe we'll begin shipping all of it this fiscal year. It's already started. I mean we're ready -- pretty much ready to go as the customer demand starts ramping now. Many of these, they have to transition between the old supply and the new supplier. And in some cases, you have a changeover where boxes have to be changed or replaced. So -- but we are very confident that all of that $60 million will begin this year. On the $25 million, that's incremental to the $60 million, similar story. That $25 million is very advanced discussions. The $60 million is firm commitments.

The $25 million is a very advanced discussions with the expectations. And we believe we can get to hopefully all of that $25 million by year-end as well, but that's going to be a little later in the year. There may be some of that, that goes into the following year. And then we've got a significant backlog lined up for next year, and that excludes the Centric opportunity. The Centric opportunity is really shaping up. There's a number of very large players that are interested in it. And certainly, we're evaluating how and what the most productive way is for us to launch that program, in particular, in light of the Quality-Built program that we already have out there.

That's doing quite well. So we'll see how that unfolds. More news or more guidance on that to come still as we get through that.

Derek Soderberg: Got it. And sticking to this -- sticking to the $60 million new business, is this accretive to gross margin? And David, I don't know if you can talk a little bit about kind of the near-term gross margin target or give us maybe some commentary on like a normalized gross margin target maybe for next fiscal year. Just maybe talk about kind of the pricing, what you're seeing on that front in this kind of maybe softer market, what we should expect on -- how should we expect -- how should we think about gross margin kind of from here?

David Lee: That's a good question. So with the additional business, gross margin should be comparable to what we've been reporting. So if we look at the most recent history, including last fiscal year, if you go through the tables in the back of our earnings press release where we exclude the items that impact the results that are noncash we've been averaging about 22-plus percent on gross margin. So we expect that when we bring on the new business, it's going to be comparable. However, with the increasing volume that we're adding and the overhead absorption that's going to be favorable and continued focus on cost reductions, we do expect to see accretion in the margins.

Operator: We have reached the end of our question-and-answer session. I will now turn the call back to Selwyn Joffe for closing remarks.

Selwyn Joffe: Well, I just want to thank everyone for their questions. I'd like to close by reinforcing a few important points. We recognize that our near-term results have been affected by delayed customer orders. We are focused on addressing these challenges and improving operating performance. At the same time, we believe the company's competitive position continues to strengthen. Our nearly $60 million in new annualized business commitments will generate additional revenue as these programs launch and ramp. We also see further growth potential through Centric Parts, the geographic expansion of our major customers, our rotating electrical diagnostic equipment business and our improved heavy-duty manufacturing platform and business.

We believe these initiatives provide multiple avenues for revenue growth, greater operating efficiencies and improved profitability. Our priorities remain clear: execute the new business launches, support our customers, improve margins, generate cash and create long-term shareholder value. I want to thank our employees for their continued dedication and our shareholders for their support, and we look forward to updating you on our progress during our next earnings call. Thank you, everyone.

Operator: Before we conclude today's call, we have one final question from George Berman with Cabot Lodge Securities.

George Berman: I'd say congratulations, a very elaborative conference call, and we'll be looking to use today's market price to add to our position substantially. Question I have is with the recent election now over, is there -- if we have any anticipated reduction in the tariff situation between U.S. and Canada, U.S. and Mexico, would that have a positive influence for you?

Selwyn Joffe: Well, clearly, I think the challenge that's out there today is that the cost of repair for the consumer has gone up substantially, in particular, in light of the tariff pass-throughs that have gone through. So to the extent the consumer can repair the vehicle for a lesser cost for them, our margins basically remain unchanged because we would reduce our prices to reflect the reduction in the tariffs. But the volume and the demand at the consumer level, I believe, will accelerate dramatically. So I think that's a very positive event. In particular, when you talk about the significant role that we play in selling new units, not only remanufactured new units.

And most of our remanufactured product is exempt because it's coming out of Mexico. But we're fast becoming leaders in the new unit business, both for brake calipers and for rotating electrical. And those are made in our Malaysia facilities, which are extremely efficient, but they have the burden of bearing some tariffs. So to the extent that those tariffs come off, it will be very advantageous to pricing and to our margins.

George Berman: Great. Maybe another quick question on Mexico. Over the last few quarters, you've alluded to the fact that Mexico is growing quite nicely for you. I saw that one of your customers, AutoZone has recently been also expanding into Brazil. Do you see the South American market in general being another growth opportunity for you?

Selwyn Joffe: That's a great question. I mean what's happening is because of the success in Mexico and all of the South American trade contracts and free enterprise zones between different countries between Mexico and South America as well as AutoZone going into Brazil, we think South America is probably the biggest opportunity as far as a new continent for us. Our Mexico sales are growing significantly, and we're seeing a lot of Mexican interest in them wanting to export into South America, which opens the door for us to move into South America as well. I think another exciting part of that is that our diagnostics equipment is all bilingual.

It's not bilingual, but right now, trilingual, but we have the flexibility of even adding Portuguese to our diagnostics. The diagnostics capability in the rotating electrical segment for us is extremely strong. And right now, to the best of my knowledge, we are the only tester that's available that can actually test the communication protocols. So to the extent you don't test communication protocols, you're getting false -- you may get false positives on testing. So having these testing units in locations where rotating electrical alternators and starters are sold is critical. And we're fast reaching the point where we have a majority of the locations in the United States.

We still have a lot more to go, but significant demand there. We have the same demand brewing in Mexico, the same demand brewing in Canada, where we have French and English and obviously, Spanish in Mexico. The diagnostics demand is -- continues to go up, and that's a pretty exciting opportunity as we get into multiple. And then the rotating electrical, I mean, we are one of the -- we have one of the broadest product offerings and our cataloging capabilities allow us to be able to reach these international markets fairly quickly and with a breadth that I think is world leading.

So I appreciate that question, but I definitely think that as you look into the future, that's a big growth opportunity. The other side is the Centric formulations. If you look at the formulations and the acceptance and the amount of Centric out at a time is around $400 million in revenue. And these brake pads, in particular, that unique formulation of these pads is so highly accepted by the installer that we have no doubt that as they start reaching reintroduced into the United States, which we already see the research that the installers are waiting to see this product, especially the professional installer market.

But we think that the applicability as we move into Mexico and other countries on the brake product line and the utilization of the Centric as well as our Quality-Built, we see a big opportunity across our whole product line spectrum in these new countries. So it's very exciting again for the future.

George Berman: And one quick housekeeping question. How many shares have you bought back in the current quarter? I saw that your interest costs are coming down dramatically as well.

Selwyn Joffe: That is true. Our interest cost -- I mean, unfortunately, that interest cost comes down because some of the sales is lower, and we don't use the supply chain finance programming as much. But we still got $20 million available on our buyback. We bought back, I mean, over -- I think, over $11 million or $12 million. David, more than that, what do we have?

David Lee: As of June 30, the trailing 12 months was about $11 million.

Selwyn Joffe: A little over $11 million. So we have still another $20 million in the current authorization available. And so we're optimistic about our potential and our future, and we continue to keep that as a potential for capital allocation.

George Berman: And I think you do have a poison pill in place, right?

Selwyn Joffe: No, we do not have a poison pill.

George Berman: That might be something you want to think about because it seems to me the equity valuation is extremely low right now.

Selwyn Joffe: Yes. Well, I certainly agree with that, yes. We'll take that under consideration. I appreciate that.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. This concludes today's call. Thank you for attending. You may now disconnect.

#3168. Wendy’s Just Released a Video Game Where You Can Win Fast Food

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

I won a medium fries by defeating a sinister robot that looked suspiciously similar to a McDonald’s french fry container.

Wendy’s has turned its red-headed mascot into a wisecracking warrior who battles evil french fry robots in a free mobile game called WendyQuest. The company announced the retro-style role-playing game on Nov. 4. The announcement came with a promotion where you can win codes in the game, which are redeemable for menu items like fries and burgers at Wendy’s locations.

WendyQuest is available to download on iOS and Android. Desktop users can get it through the Steam platform. Anyone can play the game, but the promotion is restricted to people who are 18 and up living in the US.

You need to sign up for a Wendy’s account to redeem a code. While the food you can win is free, it requires you to buy something when you go.

“Wendy’s has been a part of gaming culture for years, including on Twitch, Fortnite and Feast of Legends, but WendyQuest is the brand’s first fully owned video game,” a spokesperson for Wendy’s said.

In 2019, Wendy’s partnered with the online multiplayer video game Fortnite, as well as the video-streaming platform Twitch, for various promotions featuring the company’s mascot. The company even released a rule book for a traditional tabletop roleplaying game the same year, called Feast of Legends, as a free download.

I downloaded WendyQuest, and my daughter and I played it for a while. The blocky graphics are reminiscent of the home-console video games of the late 1980s and early 1990s. It plays a lot like a simplified version of the DragonQuest, Final Fantasy and Breath of Fire games from the era, only stuffed with fast-food branding.

Rather than the regular turn-based battles that come standard in the early RPGs, this game adds a timing element, where you need to press a button at the right time like you do in old golfing video games.

It’s not a bad game. The light humor is suitable for younger players, and it’s fun to play. Like many RPGs, you battle monsters to gain levels, search around the maps for hidden areas, buy items and talk to people in towns to figure out what’s going on.

It took us over an hour to complete the first region, Fryshire, and get the Fry Stone, which unlocks a promo code for medium fries, free with a purchase. But again, you have to sign up for a Wendy’s account on their website or on the company’s mobile app.

Video games have a long history of offering real-world prizes to players as promotions. Swordquest, a series of video games released in the early 1980s for the Atari 2600, famously held a contest where players tried to win actual treasure made of gold and jewels.

In 2015, a promotion for the video game Just Cause 3 offered players the chance to win a private island. Developer Square Enix clarified that it couldn’t guarantee that the island would be livable and that the winner would have to pay all the taxes involved.

The reward codes from WendyQuest expire seven days after you get them, and Wendy’s says the codes are first come, first served.

#3167. 6 default Pixel 11 settings I changed that made a big difference – and why

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

If you’re a new Pixel 11 user, here are six things I recommend changing right away to get the most from your phone.

I’ve been a dedicated Pixel user since the beginning, so I was naturally excited to get my hands on Google’s latest iteration, the Pixel 11 Pro XL. I’ve been impressed with it overall, but I noticed that, as Google has done before, the device isn’t set up perfectly out of the box.

Also: Pixel 11 is $200 off in this early Black Friday deal

After spending a few weeks with the device, I found that several features are either turned off by default or need optimizing to work in the best way possible.

If you’re a new Pixel 11 user, here are six things I recommend changing right away to get the most from your phone.

The camera was the biggest reason I first joined team Pixel back in 2016, so it’s one of the first places I looked on the Pixel 11 Pro XL. New this year is Camera Looks, a setting that changes how images will be processed before you take them. You can change a number of settings, including contrast, shadows, tint, sharpness, and warmth.

Also: A week with the Pixel 11 changed my mind about Gemini

I’ve always loved the camera on any Pixel I’ve had, but I’ll admit that images can look a little over-processed at times. If picture quality is important to you at all, it’s vital to set this feature right out of the box because it applies to every image you take from that point on. You can find Camera Look by opening the camera app, tapping the settings icon in the bottom-right corner, and making your changes.

Pixel’s “At a Glance” lock screen widgets are one of the most sneakily useful features, and you’re missing out if you’re not using them. These widgets are off by default, but when you enable them, you can see real-time information without unlocking your phone. You can see weather info, sports updates, flight information, rideshare and food delivery updates, fitness information, and more.

Also: These tech gifts topped our experts’ 2026 holiday wish lists

To use these widgets, long-press on an open space on your home screen. To customize your widgets, go to Settings > Wallpaper & style > More lock screen settings > Widgets on lock screen. To access your widgets, you just swipe left from your lock screen.

Out of the box, your Pixel 11’s display isn’t set to utilize its full capability. The Pixel 11 series comes with a fantastic low-temperature polycrystalline oxide (LTPO) display, but it’s slightly throttled in the name of battery life. You’ll notice the increased resolution most on text and in fine details. It won’t make a huge difference to your streaming or large display elements, though. If you read consistently, either articles or e-books, you’ll want to make the change.

To change this, head to Settings > Display > Screen Resolution. Bump the setting from “High resolution,” which is 1080 x 2404, to “Max resolution,” which is 1344 x 2992.

If you’re anything like me, your phone usually needs a quick charge some evenings. The Pixel 11 series introduced Extreme Charging Mode, which accelerates charging by pausing background activity and non-essential apps. Google says the mode should charge the Pixel 11 and 11 Pro to over 50% in 30 minutes, and the Pixel 11 Pro XL to 75% in 30 minutes. From my testing, that estimate was pretty accurate.

Also: After testing the Pixel 11, I feel fine about skipping the Pro models

There are a few caveats: this feature is only available when your phone is at or below 50% battery, and you do need to turn it on every time you use it. But after the first time you do it, it’s available in your quick settings. Head to Settings > Battery & charging > Extreme Charging to turn it on the first time.

If you have the newest Pixel, you might as well take advantage of one of its biggest selling points. I felt like this feature was gimmicky at first (and I’m still a little grumpy it replaced my beloved thermometer), but the more I use it, the more I like it. The multicolor LED on the phone’s rear camera bump can indicate who’s calling, serve as a status indicator for Gemini, and more — and it’s almost certain that more usability will arrive over time.

Where I found the most use was when I had my phone on silent. After assigning specific colors to contacts (you can do this from the contact information screen), I could easily see whether a call was worth picking up without reaching for my phone.

To make sure you’re getting the most out of your new device, head in and change your contact HiLight colors right away. It only takes a few seconds and makes deciding whether to answer a call a lot easier.

We’ve all accidentally swiped away an important notification or missed a notification in a sea of updates. The Pixel 11 offers two notification features to help you stay on top of things.

Notification History is a feature that logs every alert from the last 24 hours, including those you swipe away. This is off by default, meaning when you dismiss a notification, it’s gone forever. With this on, you get a searchable, chronological backup.

Also: Google’s big flagship is more Pro than ever

AI Notification Summaries, as the name implies, takes long multi-notification threads and stacked notifications and turns them into bullet points. This feature is powered by on-device Gemini Intelligence, and you can choose which apps to summarize.

You can find both of these under Settings > Notifications > Notification history & Notification Summaries.
